title: Three Oscillators and Strange Things
summary: Build three oscillators, join them with a diode network, shape them with an adjustable high-pass filter, then explore voltage starving, static and strange sounds.

subs.text: Connect the power rails on both sides with two jumpers at the right end of the breadboard.
Place the 40106 chip across the center gap, then add its power and ground jumpers.
Add a trimmer and two short red jumpers.
Add a large capacitor: the first oscillator is slow.
Add a second trimmer and two red jumpers at the top.
Add a small capacitor on the top rail: the second oscillator makes a tone.
Add two more red jumpers, a third trimmer and a capacitor at the bottom: the third oscillator.
Add a ground jumper from the top rail for the audio jack.
Add a long wire with a free end to use as a probe.
Insert the audio jack.
Plug in the audio cable.
Clip the battery connector onto the 9V battery.
Plug the battery wires into the top power rail.
Touch the probe to the first oscillator and listen.
Touch the probe to the second oscillator.
Touch the probe to the third oscillator.
Rest the probe by the jack. All three oscillators are ready.
Add a diode from the first oscillator's output to a shared point by the chip.
Add a diode from the second oscillator to the same point.
Add a diode from the third oscillator: all three are now combined.
Touch the probe to the point where the three diodes meet to hear the combined signal.
Listen to all three oscillators at once.
Run an orange wire from the diode network to the upper half of the board.
Add a small capacitor across the center gap. It lets only the higher sounds through.
Add a short jumper beside it.
Plug the free end of the yellow probe wire into the row after the filter. Now the filter feeds the jack.
Add a trimmer to ground and turn it to choose how much of the low sound is cut.
Unplug the battery's red (+) wire.
Add a short jumper from the + rail.
Add a trimmer next to it.
Plug the red wire into the trimmer, so all the power passes through it, and turn it slowly to starve the circuit.
Pull out the third oscillator's small capacitor (the one below the bottom rail). Without it the oscillator runs wild and the circuit makes static.
Remove the three diodes. The oscillators are no longer connected, yet turning one knob still changes the others: parts of a circuit affect each other even when disconnected.
